coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 (140–150 bpm max), sub-7:30/mi pace. You're in taper week 20 with 56 days to Slovenia, and your resting HR jumped to 79 bpm (vs. 30-day avg of 62.4)—that's a red flag for incomplete recovery. Your recovery score is 53/100 (moderate), not optimal. Skip any tempo or vert work today; this is a shakeout run only. Treat it as a confidence builder and active recovery before Saturday's long run. Given your travel schedule, run early before work if possible to lock it in.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat a full breakfast (carbs + protein: oats + eggs, or toast + Greek yogurt) 90 minutes before the run. During the easy 8–10 miler, no fuel needed. Post-run, hit a 3:1 carb-to-protein window within 30 minutes (banana + protein shake, or rice cakes + chicken). For the rest of the day, prioritize carb-loading lightly—aim for 5–6g carbs per kg bodyweight daily. You're in taper, not calorie-cutting; fuel supports recovery and glycogen supercompensation into race week.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep quality was solid last night (9.34h, 80.2% efficiency), but your elevated resting HR suggests systemic fatigue. Prioritize 9+ hours again tonight. Hydrate aggressively today—aim for 3.5–4L of fluids with electrolytes, especially given your corporate travel pattern. Consider 10 minutes of foam rolling on quads and calves post-run, then a 15-minute walk or gentle mobility work. Skip ice baths; passive recovery and sleep are your tools in taper.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You've logged 47.4 miles in two weeks (taper is working—down from peak phases), and your recent long runs (17+ miles with 374 ft vert at Z3) prove you can handle Julian Alps' demands. The slight fatigue you're showing is normal mid-taper; it will clear by race day. Use today's easy run to remind yourself of your fitness—don't second-guess the training done. Focus on execution and logistics: map aid stations, test your race-day pack, confirm drop bags with the race org. Mental sharpness beats panic now.
